decision.title: The built-in schemas are an optional feature; the core size guard (packet health-3)
decision.summary: The processor's built-in schemas become the optional feature "builtin-schemas", taking the XSD schema compiler out of the core sxml.wasm again, with FODC0014 or FOJS0004 where validation would need them.

body.p: , after , , , . The core sxml.wasm was 2,352,234 bytes stripped (823,283 gzipped) at 6130546, over 's 2,200,000 / 770,000, so javascript/size_budget failed again.

item.p: What grew it (linker maps of the core module per commit, code and data, from ae7ef0b at 2,131,859): c008c7c (packet , lax validation without in-scope schemas) +171,516: plan_validation called sxml_processor_get_builtin_schema, which runs sxml_schema_create, so the whole XSD schema compiler was reachable from XPath again, as found for DTD validation: schema_read 43,074, schema_content_model 26,932, schema_simple_type 18,108, schema_complex_type 18,062, schema_resolve 9,475, schema_assemble 9,055, schema_components 4,736, schema_assertion 3,689, schema_identity 2,457, data 21,853. 820231e (the fn: schema, D.1 to D.3) made it reachable a second way. d326dcc (7.6b) +18,136: evaluator_stream 14,565, linked through the evaluator part registry () although only XSLT lowers to STREAM. 4d78eba (xml-mem) +8,697: document segments and the XML grammar's tables. 29aff55 (fn:element-to-map) +5,347; 1fd0615 (7.17's core part of the formatting functions) +4,703; 3c8b502 (deep-equal options) +1,888; f164846 +2,070; 81728fb +1,674 (Full Text lowering through the registry, ); 658ad10 +1,577; 820231e +1,370; the rest under 1,000. No feature definition was linked into the core by mistake.

Moved: the processor's built-in schemas for XPath's functions become sxml_builtin_schemas_feature() (include/sxml/schema.h, additive; name "builtin-schemas"; kind SXML_OPTIONAL_FEATURE_KIND_BUILTIN_SCHEMAS; definition in src/processor_builtin_schemas.c, operations type in src/processor_internal.h). src/function_library_schema.c reaches sxml_processor_get_builtin_schema and sxml_processor_get_function_namespace_schema only through the table. Without the feature ('s place): lax validation of fn:doc and fn:parse-xml without an in-scope schema raises FODC0014 as strict does (as before c008c7c); fn:json-to-xml validate=true without an in-scope schema of the fn: namespace raises FOJS0004, F&O 4.0's error for a processor that cannot validate (17.4.6); fn:analyze-string's result stays untyped (6.3.4: implementation-defined). XQuery's and XSLT's in-scope schemas call the getters directly and do not need the feature. sxml_all_optional_features() includes it, so the sxml command, the drivers and sxml-full.wasm are unchanged.

Guard: the JavaScript modules are linked with a map (-Wl,-Map, beside each module), and size-budget.mjs compares the core's map with bindings/javascript/test/size-baseline/sxml.txt (code and data per object at this audit): it prints the five largest growths on every run and twenty when the core is over budget, so the object and the commit are named at once. A packet that raises a budget or audits the core refreshes the baseline in the same change (node size-budget.mjs --write-baseline MAP BASELINE).
Not moved (owned by running packets): evaluator_stream 14,565 (7.6c; a registry split by language, 's 75 KB, would drop it with the XQuery lowering parts).

Sizes: sxml.wasm 2,352,234 / 823,283 to 2,180,960 / 762,788, under 2,200,000 / 770,000 with no core budget raised. sxml-full.wasm was 7,002,841 / 1,595,270, over its 7,000,000 (Full Text's stemmers, stop words and thesauri, 7.12b/c; 2.22's schema work): its budget rises to 7,500,000 / 2,625,000 (, ratio 0.35). javascript/package_full lists invisible-xml, localization and builtin-schemas, which its feature list lacked.

Same pass: debug-gcc failed in src/function_library_binary.c (-Wconversion on a conditional over two uint8_t operands, whose type is int, C17 6.5.15p5); GCC sees it only under -fsanitize=undefined, so a plain command line did not show it. tools/run-wasi.mjs preopens /usr/share/zoneinfo, so cli/xpath_timezone passes under WASI. The goldens of cli/validate_not_well_formed and cli/validate_schema_not_well_formed follow 's segmented parse: a document that ends inside an element gets the parser's truncation message at the same place, and the validity errors before the fatal error are reported too (XML 1.0, 1.2).
